title: 2.5.19 Reject the Bad Input
description: Throw an error when a password is too short, and catch it with a clear message. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Set up the password
steps.instructions: Create a constant called password set to "abc".

steps.title: Check the length and throw
steps.instructions: Inside a try block, if password.length is less than 8, throw new Error with a message saying the password must be at least 8 characters. Otherwise log "Password accepted".

steps.title: Catch and report
steps.instructions: In the catch block, log err.message. Test with "abc", then change password to a longer value and confirm it logs "Password accepted" instead.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[set password to abc]
  B --> C{shorter than 8 characters}
  C -- yes --> D[throw an error]
  D --> E[/log the error message/]
  C -- no --> F[no error is thrown]
  F --> H[/log Password accepted/]
  E --> G([End])
  H --> G

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.5.19 Reject the Bad Input". The task they were given: Create a constant called password set to "abc". You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
